entity.summary: South Korean centralized cryptocurrency exchange offering KRW trading markets and cryptocurrency deposit/withdrawal services. On 2026-11-06 it temporarily suspended deposits, normal withdrawals and trading after receiving a hacking-threat email, while arranging manually reviewed withdrawals through support; no asset theft from this threat was confirmed at the time.
entity.notes: 2026-11-06: GOPAX received an email threatening a hack. Deposits and standard withdrawals were suspended from 14:55 KST and trading from 15:53 KST; pending orders were canceled. Assets were being moved to cold wallets. Customer-support withdrawals require manual verification/approval; resumption timing was not announced. Multiple same-day reports quoting GOPAX said no actual hack or theft was confirmed in this incident. Status is limited because normal trading and transfer functions are halted but manual withdrawal support remains. Do not classify as dead, hacked, insolvent, or as confirmed asset loss based on the threat email alone. Existing official platform/API evidence is retained as historical identity documentation; it does not establish current transaction availability. Direct GOPAX notice URL was not independently resolved in this review.

events.title: GOPAX temporarily halted deposits and standard withdrawals after hack threat
events.description: After receiving a threatening email from an alleged hacker, GOPAX stopped cryptocurrency deposits and standard website/app withdrawals from 14:55 KST. Customer-service requests for manual withdrawals remained possible subject to internal verification. The exchange began moving assets to cold wallets; no confirmed theft from this incident was reported.
events.notes: Preemptive security suspension, not evidence of a successful hack or a permanent shutdown. Coinone issued a contemporaneous warning about inbound GOPAX transfers.

events.title: GOPAX suspended cryptocurrency trading and canceled outstanding orders
events.description: GOPAX halted cryptocurrency trading at 15:53 KST on 2026-11-06 and canceled all outstanding unfilled orders. The decision followed a hacking-threat email and security precautions, with no announced service-resumption date or confirmed theft from the reported threat.
events.notes: The event is trading_halted, not hack; the threatening email had not been independently authenticated.

evidence.title: GOPAX official exchange
evidence.notes: Current first-party GOPAX exchange endpoint is reachable and identifies the service as a Korean virtual-asset exchange.

evidence.title: GOPAX REST API
evidence.notes: Official GOPAX REST API documentation covers KRW trading pairs, balances, order queries, market and limit order placement, cancellation, trade history, deposits and withdrawals, tickers, order books, market statistics, charts, notices, WebSocket access, and a change history extending to 2026-06-02.

evidence.title: GOPAX API Documentation repository
evidence.notes: Official GOPAX GitHub organization repository points users to the GOPAX API documentation and provides first-party ownership linkage for the documented trading API.

evidence.title: Notice: Caution regarding withdrawals to GOPAX
evidence.notes: First-party warning from another Korean exchange, confirming GOPAX deposits and withdrawals were suspended from 14:55 KST and incoming GOPAX deposits might not be credited normally; it is not a GOPAX-issued notice.

evidence.title: GOPAX suspends withdrawals following hacking threats
evidence.notes: Confirms 14:55 KST withdrawal suspension, cold-wallet transfers, and GOPAX's statement that no actual asset loss had been reported.

evidence.title: Gopax halts withdrawals, trading after receiving hacking threat email
evidence.notes: Reports 15:53 KST trading halt, canceled open orders, no confirmed hack or asset loss, and no defined resumption schedule.

evidence.title: Gopax Crypto Exchange Suspends Withdrawals, Trading After Receiving Hacker Threat
evidence.notes: Corroborates trading halt and cancellation of pending orders at 15:53 KST. GOPAX representative said this was a precautionary measure and no actual hacking incident had occurred.
